Signed 64-bit time value representing durations or timestamps in microseconds (us). Used across the API for time intervals and absolute times. Underlying type is int64_t.

Abstract interface for time-related operations. Provides a virtual usleep method to suspend execution for the specified microsecond duration. Concrete implementations are defined elsewhere. Construction and destruction are via the declared constructor/destructor; as a pure interface, instances are typically created through derived classes. Other behavioral details are not specified here.

A small value-type wrapper around a context identifier string used for correlating operations. Provides string access (c_str), emptiness check, comparison, and setter. Ownership is straightforward; it contains an internal std::string. The SRS_DECLARE_PRIVATE macro may expose members as public in unit-test builds, but normally v_ is private. Construct with default or copy; destruction is trivial. Aliased as SrsContextId for public API.

functions.name: srs_time_since
functions.description: Computes a time duration in microseconds as end - start. If either start or end is 0, the function returns 0. Intended for measuring intervals when timestamps are expressed in srs_utime_t (microseconds).
requirements: Inputs start and end are timestamps/durations in microseconds (type srs_utime_t).
If start == 0 or end == 0, the function returns 0 (per comment).
Caller should ensure start and end are comparable (same time base) to get a meaningful positive/negative duration. (Inferred)

functions.name: srs_time_now_cached
functions.description: Returns the current system time as srs_utime_t (microseconds), using a cached value to reduce performance overhead of frequent time queries.
requirements: No explicit preconditions are documented.
Returned time unit is microseconds (srs_utime_t).
The value may be slightly stale due to caching. (Inferred from description)

functions.name: srs_time_since_startup
functions.description: Returns the time in microseconds (srs_utime_t) since the process (or system component) startup. Exact reference (process vs. system) is not documented; inferred as process startup based on name.
requirements: No explicit preconditions are documented.
Returned unit is microseconds (srs_utime_t).
Reference point is startup; callers should not assume wall-clock time. (Inferred)

functions.name: srs_time_now_realtime
functions.description: Returns the current real-time clock in microseconds (srs_utime_t). A daemon st-thread updates the underlying cached value.
requirements: No explicit preconditions are documented.
Returned unit is microseconds (srs_utime_t).
Accuracy depends on update frequency of the daemon st-thread; may be slightly delayed. (Inferred from comment)

functions.name: ISrsTime::ISrsTime
functions.description: Constructor for the ISrsTime interface, which defines a time-related abstraction (e.g., sleeping). Typically used as a base class for concrete time providers.
requirements: No explicit preconditions are documented.
As an interface constructor, it should be invoked via construction of a derived class; ISrsTime itself is abstract.

functions.name: ISrsTime::~ISrsTime
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the ISrsTime interface to ensure proper cleanup through base-class pointers.
requirements: No explicit preconditions are documented.
Derived classes must ensure any resources are released safely in their destructors.

functions.name: ISrsTime::usleep
functions.description: Pure virtual method to sleep for the specified duration in microseconds. Implementations should block the calling thread for approximately duration microseconds.
requirements: duration is specified in microseconds (srs_utime_t).
duration should be non-negative; negative values are not meaningful. (Inferred)
Function may block the calling thread; callers should not hold locks that could cause deadlocks during sleep. (General concurrency caution, inferred)
Must be implemented by derived classes; calling through an abstract instance is not possible.

functions.name: SrsUniquePtr::SrsUniquePtr
functions.signature: template <class T> SrsUniquePtr<T>::SrsUniquePtr(T* ptr = NULL, void (*deleter)(T*) = NULL)
functions.description: Constructs a unique-ownership smart pointer managing a single T object. If a custom deleter is provided, it will be used to dispose the managed pointer on destruction; otherwise delete is used.
requirements: ptr must point to an object allocated with new if no deleter is provided
If a custom deleter is provided, it must be callable as void(T*) and must correctly free the resource that ptr points to (e.g., for malloc-allocated memory, provide a matching free)
Do not pass pointers to arrays or memory allocated by malloc unless a correct deleter is supplied (non-array specialization uses delete by default)
ptr may be NULL; however, dereferencing via operator-> or operator* requires it to be non-NULL

functions.name: SrsUniquePtr::~SrsUniquePtr
functions.description: Destructor for the unique pointer managing a single object. Disposes the managed pointer using the provided deleter if set; otherwise uses delete.
requirements: The managed object must be valid for deletion by the chosen deleter (custom deleter if provided, otherwise delete)
After destruction, the managed pointer must not be used elsewhere (unique ownership is assumed)

functions.name: SrsUniquePtr::get
functions.description: Returns the raw managed pointer without transferring ownership. Safe to call even if no object is managed (returns NULL).
requirements: Caller must not delete or free the returned pointer
Caller must not assume the pointer remains valid beyond the lifetime of the SrsUniquePtr instance
The returned pointer may be NULL; caller must check before dereferencing

functions.name: SrsUniquePtr::operator->
functions.description: Provides pointer-like access to the managed object to call its members.
requirements: The managed pointer must be non-NULL before calling operator-> to avoid a crash
The managed object must be valid and properly initialized

functions.name: SrsUniquePtr<T[]>::SrsUniquePtr
functions.description: Constructs a unique-ownership smart pointer managing an array of T allocated with new[]. Uses delete[] on destruction.
requirements: ptr must point to an array allocated with new[]
ptr may be NULL; however, operator[] requires non-NULL and a valid index
Do not pass pointers allocated by malloc or to single objects (this specialization deletes with delete[])

functions.name: SrsUniquePtr<T[]>::~SrsUniquePtr
functions.description: Destructor for the unique pointer managing an array of T. Disposes the managed array using delete[].
requirements: The managed pointer must be valid for deletion by delete[]
After destruction, the managed pointer must not be used elsewhere (unique ownership is assumed)

functions.name: SrsUniquePtr<T[]>::get
functions.description: Returns the raw pointer to the managed array without transferring ownership.
requirements: Caller must not delete[] or free the returned pointer
The returned pointer may be NULL; caller must check before use
Bounds checking is the caller's responsibility when accessing elements

functions.name: SrsUniquePtr<T[]>::operator[]
functions.description: Provides non-const indexed access to the managed array element at the given index.
requirements: The managed pointer must be non-NULL
index must be within the allocated array bounds (no bounds checking is performed)
The referenced element must be valid to modify

functions.name: SrsUniquePtr<T[]>::operator[]
functions.signature: template <class T> const T& SrsUniquePtr<T[]>::operator[](std::size_t index) const
functions.description: Provides const indexed access to the managed array element at the given index.
requirements: The managed pointer must be non-NULL
index must be within the allocated array bounds (no bounds checking is performed)

functions.name: SrsSharedPtr::SrsSharedPtr
functions.description: Constructs a reference-counted shared smart pointer managing a single T object, initializing the reference count to 1.
requirements: ptr must point to an object suitable for deletion by delete (no custom deleter supported)
ptr may be NULL; dereferencing via operator-> or operator* requires it to be non-NULL

functions.name: SrsSharedPtr::SrsSharedPtr
functions.description: Copy constructor. Shares ownership of the managed object and increments the reference count.
requirements: cp may manage NULL; dereferencing requires non-NULL
After construction, both instances share the same ownership and deletion will occur when the last reference is destroyed or reset

functions.name: SrsSharedPtr::SrsSharedPtr
functions.description: Move constructor (C++11 and later). Transfers ownership and reference counter pointers from cp to this, leaving cp empty.
requirements: Requires C++11 or later (__cplusplus >= 201103L)
cp is left in an empty state (ptr_ == NULL, ref_count_ == NULL) after the move; caller must not use cp expecting it to still own the object

functions.name: SrsSharedPtr::~SrsSharedPtr
functions.description: Destructor. Decrements the reference count; deletes the managed object and the reference counter when the count reaches zero.
requirements: The managed object must be valid for deletion by delete
After destruction, this instance must not be used; remaining shared instances (if any) continue to own the object

functions.name: SrsSharedPtr::get
functions.description: Returns the raw managed pointer without altering ownership or the reference count.
requirements: Caller must not delete the returned pointer
Pointer may be NULL; caller must check before dereferencing

functions.name: SrsSharedPtr::operator->
functions.description: Provides pointer-like access to the managed object to call its members.
requirements: The managed pointer must be non-NULL before calling operator->
The managed object must be valid and properly initialized

functions.name: SrsSharedPtr::operator=
functions.signature: template <class T> SrsSharedPtr<T>& SrsSharedPtr<T>::operator=(const SrsSharedPtr<T>& cp)
functions.description: Copy assignment. Releases current ownership (decrementing its count) and shares ownership of cp, incrementing its reference count.
requirements: Self-assignment is handled; no special action required by caller
Both pointers may be NULL; dereferencing requires non-NULL after assignment

functions.name: SrsSharedPtr::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment (C++11 and later). Releases current ownership and transfers ownership and reference counter from cp, leaving cp empty.
requirements: Requires C++11 or later (__cplusplus >= 201103L)
After the move, cp must not be used expecting it to still own the object

functions.name: _SrsContextId::c_str
functions.description: Returns a NUL-terminated C-string view of the current context ID value for interoperability with C APIs. Pointer remains valid until the object is modified or destroyed.

functions.name: _SrsContextId::compare

requirements: Parameter to must be a valid _SrsContextId reference.
Comparison is case-sensitive and locale-independent (inferred from std::string semantics).
No side effects; safe to call on const instances.

functions.description: Sets the context ID to the provided string value and returns *this, allowing fluent chaining. Use to assign or update the current identifier.

data_types.description: A generic byte string with no format constraints. May contain any bytes including ASCII, Unicode, control characters, or NULs when represented as a std::string. Used wherever a function accepts an unconstrained string value for storage or comparison.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid arbitrary strings for _SrsContextId related fuzzers.
# The fuzzers consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR (std::string) and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int).
# Our bytes buffer should encode a sequence of interesting strings and integers
# that the harness will read in order. We don't know the exact input demuxing,
# so we provide a compact self-describing stream of entries:
# [entry_count:u16][entries...]
# Each entry is either a string or a 32-bit unsigned int:
#   For string:  tag=0x01, len:u16, data:len bytes
#   For uint32:  tag=0x02, value:u32 (little-endian)
# Strings may contain arbitrary bytes, including NUL.
# We craft entries to cover cases: empty, ASCII, long, unicode-like utf8, binary,
# lexicographic edge cases (prefix relations), and values used by modes 0/1/2.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _u16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', x & 0xFFFF)

def _u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def _entry_str(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Cap each string length to 2048 to keep overall buffer < 4096
    b = b[:2048]
    return b"\x01" + _u16(len(b)) + b

def _entry_u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\x02" + _u32(v)

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"", b"a", b"A", b"0", b" ", b"\n", b"\t", b"abc", b"ABC", b"AaBbCc",
    b"hello", b"world", b"prefix", b"prefix_longer", b"same", b"SAME",
    b"caseSensitive", b"casesensitive", b"zzz", b"zz", b"z",
]

UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    "こんにちは".encode('utf-8'),
    "😊".encode('utf-8'),
    "ß".encode('utf-8'),
    "Ångström".encode('utf-8'),
    "Μετά".encode('utf-8'),
]

BINARY_SAMPLES = [
    b"\x00", b"\x00\x00", b"\x00end", b"mid\x00nul", b"\xff", b"\x7f\x80\xff",
]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-\n\t"
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _lex_prefix_pair(base: bytes) -> (bytes, bytes):
    # Ensure s1 < s2 by making s2 = base + 0xFF if possible
    return base, base + b"\xff"

def _long_sample(rng: random.Random, min_len=256, max_len=1800) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix ASCII and binary
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    while len(b"".join(chunks)) < n:
        choice = rng.randint(0, 2)
        if choice == 0:
            chunks.append(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(8, 64)))
        elif choice == 1:
            chunks.append(rng.randbytes(rng.randint(4, 32)))
        else:
            chunks.append(b"\x00")
    data = b"".join(chunks)[:n]
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # Mode integers for fuzzers that use *FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    # Ensure coverage for compare: 0 (equal), 1 (s1 < s2), 2 (random)
    entries.append(_entry_u32(0))
    entries.append(_entry_u32(1))
    entries.append(_entry_u32(2))

    # Also add some random mode bits for operator= (self-assign vs normal)
    for _ in range(3):
        entries.append(_entry_u32(rng.getrandbits(32)))

    # Strings to cover empty and small ASCII
    for s in ASCII_WORDS:
        entries.append(_entry_str(s))

    # UTF-8 samples
    for s in UTF8_SAMPLES:
        entries.append(_entry_str(s))

    # Binary strings with NUL and high bytes
    for s in BINARY_SAMPLES:
        entries.append(_entry_str(s))

    # Lexicographic controlled pair: s1 < s2
    base = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 16))
    s1, s2 = _lex_prefix_pair(base)
    entries.append(_entry_str(s1))
    entries.append(_entry_str(s2))

    # Equal pair for compare mode 0
    eq = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 32))
    entries.append(_entry_str(eq))
    entries.append(_entry_str(eq))

    # Random pairs to let mode 2 explore both directions
    for _ in range(4):
        entries.append(_entry_str(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 40))))
        entries.append(_entry_str(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 40))))

    # Long strings to exercise memory paths and compare performance/edge
    entries.append(_entry_str(_long_sample(rng)))
    entries.append(_entry_str(_long_sample(rng)))

    # A near-maximum length string with structured pattern
    pattern = (b"CTX-" + _rand_ascii(rng, 12) + b"-\x00-\xff-")
    repeat = max(1, 1800 // max(1, len(pattern)))
    big = (pattern * repeat)[:2000]
    entries.append(_entry_str(big))

    # Random binary blobs
    for _ in range(3):
        entries.append(_entry_str(rng.randbytes(rng.randint(1, 128))))

    # Assemble with header and ensure size limit
    body = b"".join(entries)
    # Trim if necessary (avoid cutting inside an entry by re-packing downwards)
    max_body = MAX_TOTAL - 2  # reserve for entry_count
    if len(body) > max_body:
        # Keep dropping from the end until under limit
        while entries and len(b"".join(entries)) > max_body:
            entries.pop()
        body = b"".join(entries)

    count = 0
    i = 0
    while i < len(body):
        tag = body[i]
        if tag == 0x01 and i + 3 <= len(body):
            # string: tag + u16 + data
            if i + 3 > len(body):
                break
            ln = struct.unpack_from('<H', body, i + 1)[0]
            i += 3 + ln
        elif tag == 0x02 and i + 5 <= len(body):
            i += 5
        else:
            break
        count += 1

    header = _u16(count)
    return header + body[:max_body]
